name: Museum Tiroler Bauernhöfe
kurzbeschreibung: Museum Tiroler Bauernhöfe in Kramsach: Tyrol's largest open-air museum featuring 14 original farmsteads and 37 outbuildings from all parts of Tyrol across 8 hectares.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fascinating Museum Tiroler Bauernhöfe in Kramsach in the Tyrolean Unterinntal is the largest open-air museum in the province of Tyrol. Nestled into a picturesque rolling landscape near the Kramsach lakes across around eight hectares of open grounds, the museum takes its visitors on a vivid journey back in time to rural history. 14 original farmsteads and 37 historic outbuildings from various valleys of North, South, and East Tyrol were rescued from decay and painstakingly rebuilt here. The open-air museum provides authentic insights into the arduous lives and labour of Tyrolean mountain farming families over past centuries, shaped by the rhythm of nature.

History & Farmstead Ensemble

The initiative for the museum's founding came from the dedicated Kramsach teacher and local historian Heinz Mantl (1921–2014), who recognised in the 1970s the imminent loss of historic timber architecture due to modernisation. In 1974, the museum association was established, followed by the official opening in 1977. Every single building was carefully documented beam by beam at its original location in the Tyrolean valleys, dismantled, and faithfully reassembled on the museum grounds. The oldest structures date from the 15th and 16th centuries, including the Gwiggen farmstead from the Wildschönau (built in 1569) and the mighty Schrofenstein farmstead from the Tannheimer Tal. The ensembles encompass not only typical residential houses and stables with their wooden shingle roofs and carved balconies, but also working historic watermills, sawmills, a blacksmith's forge, flax-breaking huts, a village fire station, an old schoolhouse, and a baroque field chapel. Displayed inside the smoke-blackened open-hearth kitchens, cosy stone-pine parlours with masonry tile stoves, and threshing barn floors are authentic tools, looms, and traditional household furnishings. Modern video stations (“Time Travel through Old Parlours”) and historic heritage livestock breeds make the walk especially vivid.

Visit & Getting There

The Museum Tiroler Bauernhöfe is open seasonally every day from Palm Sunday / late March until late October. Opening hours: in midsummer (May to September) daily from 09:00 to 18:00 (last admission 16:30); in low season (March/April and October) daily from 09:00 to 17:00 (last admission 15:30). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €13.00, children and teenagers aged 6 to 17 €5.00, children under 6 free; family ticket (2 adults + own children) €26.00. Free admission with the regional Alpbachtal Card. Arrival by train: ÖBB to Bahnhof Brixlegg, then continue with VVT bus line 601 or 611 directly to the stop Kramsach Abzw. Tiroler Bauernhöfe (approx. three minutes' walk from there). By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Kramsach, follow signs towards the Reintaler Seen lakes (Angerberg 10; large paid car park directly at the visitor centre).

Tips

The approximately three-kilometre circular trail leads over natural gravel paths through gently rolling meadows; for wheelchairs and standard prams, an all-terrain model or strong pushing assistance is recommended (due to historic construction, the traditional wooden parlours have high door thresholds). An accessible toilet is available in the modern entrance pavilion. A fun quiz rally is available at the ticket desk for children. Stop by the historic Rohrerhof dating from 1581 right on the museum grounds to savour traditional Tyrolean Kasspatzln or Kaiserschmarrn in the outdoor beer garden.
